605.title: Revenue Recognition
605.tag: Legacy revenue Topic — nearly all guidance superseded by ASC 606; remnants for provisions for losses and non-customer contracts.
605.truth: Before 2018, US revenue rules were a patchwork of industry-specific pieces — software, construction, real estate, each with its own rulebook. ASC 606 replaced them with one five-step model. Topic 605 survives mainly as history and for a few remnants (e.g., provisions for losses on certain contracts and guidance for arrangements that are not contracts with customers).

analogy.title: The Old City Map
analogy.story: Your grandfather's city map shows streets that have since been renamed and rerouted. It's useful for understanding why a neighborhood looks the way it does, but you'd never navigate today with it. Topic 605 is that old map; ASC 606 is the GPS.

recognition: Use ASC 606 for contracts with customers; 605 remnants apply only where explicitly retained (605-10-05-3).

Legacy concepts still tested in interviews: SAB 104's four criteria (persuasive evidence, delivery, fixed/determinable fee, collectibility), VSOE for multiple elements, percentage-of-completion vs. completed-contract.
Provision for losses on separately priced extended warranty and product maintenance contracts and certain construction/production contracts remain in 605 subtopics.

measurement.initial: Transaction measurement now follows 606 (transaction price, allocation by standalone selling price).
measurement.subsequent: Loss provisions remain measured under the retained 605 guidance.

journalEntries.label: Legacy percentage-of-completion (historical illustration)
journalEntries.scenario: Under legacy 605-35, a contractor 40% complete on a $5,000,000 contract recognized $2,000,000 of revenue against $1,600,000 of cost.

lines.account: Costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings

journalEntries.memo: Today the same economics are analyzed under ASC 606 (over-time recognition with an input or output method).

auditTraps.q: Is VSOE still required to separate software elements?
auditTraps.a: No. ASC 606 allocates using standalone selling prices, which can be estimated — VSOE was eliminated.

auditTraps.q: Does 605 govern real estate sales today?
auditTraps.a: No. Sales of real estate follow ASC 606 (customers) or ASC 610-20 (nonfinancial assets to noncustomers); legacy full-accrual/deposit methods are gone.

auditTraps.q: What legacy revenue criteria are still asked in interviews?
auditTraps.a: SAB 104's four criteria — useful to contrast with 606's control-based five steps.

606.title: Revenue from Contracts with Customers
606.tag: The five-step model: revenue when control of a promised good or service transfers, at the amount you expect to be entitled to.
606.truth: Revenue is the reward for keeping a promise to a customer. So you first identify the promises (performance obligations), put a price on each, and recognize revenue as each promise is kept — at a point in time or over time as the customer gains control. Cash timing is irrelevant; variable amounts are included only to the extent a significant reversal is not probable.

analogy.title: The Gym Membership with a Personal-Training Bonus
analogy.story: A gym sells a 12-month membership plus five personal-training sessions for $1,200. The gym has made two promises. It earns the membership piece a month at a time and each training session when it happens — not all $1,200 on the day your card is charged. If you get a refund for unused sessions, that's variable consideration the gym must estimate.

recognition: Step 1 — identify the contract: approved, rights and payment terms identifiable, commercial substance, collection of substantially all consideration probable (606-10-25-1).

Step 2 — identify distinct performance obligations. Step 3 — determine the transaction price (variable consideration constrained to amounts not probable of significant reversal). Step 4 — allocate by standalone selling price. Step 5 — recognize when (or as) control transfers.

Over-time recognition if the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits, controls the asset as it's created, or the asset has no alternative use with an enforceable right to payment (606-10-25-27).
Scope excludes leases (ASC 842) — resident rent is not 606 revenue (606-10-15-2).
Principal vs. agent: gross if you control the good/service before transfer; net fee/commission if you arrange for another party.

measurement.basis: Transaction price allocated to performance obligations
measurement.initial: Initial: expected consideration including constrained variable consideration, adjusted for significant financing components and noncash consideration.
measurement.subsequent: Subsequent: update variable consideration each period; contract modifications accounted for as separate contracts, prospectively or cumulative catch-up.

journalEntries.label: Nonrefundable application/amenity fee (point in time)
journalEntries.scenario: A community collects $45,000 of nonrefundable application fees in a month for processing screening services (not a lease component).
journalEntries.memo: Screening service is delivered at application; confirm the fee is not a disguised lease payment (which would be straight-lined under 842).

journalEntries.label: Property management fee revenue (over time, variable)
journalEntries.scenario: A management company earns 3% of collected revenue; September collections are $1,400,000.
journalEntries.memo: Series of distinct daily services; variable fee allocated to the month it relates to.

auditTraps.a: No. Leases are excluded from 606 (606-10-15-2(a)); rent is lessor income under ASC 842. Non-lease services (e.g., separately contracted cleaning, some utilities) may be 606 unless combined under the lessor practical expedient.

auditTraps.q: When do you constrain variable consideration?
auditTraps.a: Include only the amount for which it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the uncertainty resolves.

auditTraps.q: A management company passes through on-site payroll reimbursements. Gross or net?
auditTraps.a: Depends on control: if the manager is the employer and controls the staff service, reimbursements are gross revenue (principal); if acting as agent, net.

auditTraps.q: Are contract assets and receivables the same?
auditTraps.a: No. A receivable is an unconditional right (only time must pass); a contract asset is conditional on something other than time (e.g., further performance).

auditTraps.q: Is selling a property to a buyer 606?
auditTraps.a: Only if the buyer is a customer (sale in the ordinary course, e.g., a homebuilder). Otherwise ASC 610-20 applies, which borrows 606's control and measurement concepts.

606.propertyLens: Property accountants apply 606 to non-lease income: application and admin fees, some utility reimbursements, laundry/vending commissions, cable/telecom revenue share, and management/leasing fees at the manager level.

610.title: Other Income
610.tag: Other income: gains on selling nonfinancial assets (610-20) and involuntary conversions (610-30).
610.truth: Selling a building you used to earn rent is not revenue from customers, but it should follow the same logic: derecognize when the buyer gets control, and measure the gain using the consideration you expect. And when fire or condemnation forces you to give up an asset, the insurer's or government's cash is a separate monetary transaction — the gain or loss is recognized even if you rebuild.

analogy.title: Selling Your Car vs. Totaling It
analogy.story: Selling your car to a neighbor: once she drives off with the keys and title, the sale is done and your gain or loss is price minus book value. If your car is totaled and the insurer pays you, that's also a 'sale' of sorts — the car turned into cash, and any gain counts even if you immediately buy a new car.

recognition: 610-20: first evaluate control under ASC 810 (if you still control the entity holding the asset, don't derecognize); then derecognize when the counterparty obtains control and a contract exists (applying 606 contract and control criteria) (610-20-25-1 to 25-3).
Partial sales: when control of a subsidiary is lost, recognize any retained noncontrolling interest at fair value.
610-30: involuntary conversions of nonmonetary assets to monetary assets are monetary transactions — recognize gain or loss even if reinvested (610-30-25-3).
Insurance proceeds above the recognized loss are gain contingencies recognized when realized.

measurement.basis: Consideration (606 transaction-price concepts) minus carrying amount
measurement.initial: Gain = consideration (including variable consideration constrained, noncash consideration at fair value) − carrying amount of assets derecognized.
measurement.subsequent: Subsequent: update variable consideration (e.g., earn-outs) with changes in gain.

journalEntries.label: Sell an apartment community (not a business, buyer is not a customer)
journalEntries.scenario: Sale price $42,000,000 less $840,000 selling costs; carrying amount: building $31,000,000, accumulated depreciation $9,500,000, land $6,000,000; the $24,000,000 mortgage is repaid from proceeds.

lines.account: Gain on sale of real estate

journalEntries.memo: Gain = 42,000,000 − 840,000 − (31,000,000 − 9,500,000 + 6,000,000) = 13,660,000. Present in continuing operations unless a strategic shift (ASC 205-20).

journalEntries.label: Insurance settlement after a fire (involuntary conversion)
journalEntries.scenario: A fire destroyed a building wing with a carrying amount of $1,100,000 (already written off to a casualty loss). The insurer settles for $1,600,000.

lines.account: Casualty loss (recovery up to loss recognized)

journalEntries.memo: Gain is recognized when the settlement is realized, even though the wing will be rebuilt.

auditTraps.a: Only if the buyer is a customer (ordinary activities). Typical dispositions by owners are 610-20 gains.

auditTraps.q: Seller retains a 20% interest in the JV that buys the property. Gain?
auditTraps.a: If control of the entity is lost, derecognize 100% and measure the retained interest at fair value — full gain (ASU 2017-05).

auditTraps.q: Can you defer the insurance gain until the building is rebuilt?
auditTraps.a: No. Involuntary conversions are monetary transactions — recognize gain when realized, even if reinvested (tax deferral under IRC §1033 is a separate matter).
A financial asset (e.g., cash in a subsidiary) promised to a counterparty in a contract where substantially all the fair value is in nonfinancial assets — it follows 610-20.

610.propertyLens: Dispositions of communities, land parcels and JV interests, plus fire and hurricane insurance settlements, are measured here.

keyParagraphs.subtopic: 20 Gains and Losses from the Derecognition of Nonfinancial Assets
keyParagraphs.excerpt: To recognize a gain or loss from the transfer of nonfinancial assets or in substance nonfinancial assets within the scope of this Subtopic, an entity shall apply the guidance in Topic 810 on consolidation and in Topic 606 on revenue from contracts with customers as described in paragraphs 610-20-25-2 through 25-7.
